messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — I'm splitting the Usage tiers doc into two pages (metering vs pricing) to reduce confusion. There's a couple of downstream dashboard links that need updating. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/827. Can reviewers sanity-check the SDK snippet and the grafana panel references?
maya: Nice, thanks. Link?
alex: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/827
jordan: On it. Two quick notes: 1) the Python SDK snippet uses the old `client.create_metering` call, should be `client.report_usage`. 2) grafana panel id 1024 was renamed to 2048 in grafana-ops during last panel move — that'll break the direct link.
samir: Re: snippet — I can open a tiny follow-up PR to update the code block. Do we want to keep both variants (legacy + current) or just the current one?
ciara: Prefer keeping both with a deprecation note. Lots of customers pin older SDKs, and having the legacy example with a clear 'deprecated' banner helps migrations.
li: For the migration guide, add a checklist: update headers, replace `X-Usage-Tier` examples, mention burst-window edge-case and token_count vs token_total in payloads. Also update example payload schemas to the new shape.
alex: Agree. I'll add the checklist to the PR description and the migration guide section.
maya: Also please clarify rate-limiter behavior when a tier cap is reached — current line says 'requests may be throttled' which is ambiguous.
jordan: I'll add a compact example showing a `429` response with `Retry-After` header and a tiny client backoff snippet:
```
# naive backoff
for attempt in range(5):
    resp = client.request(...)
    if resp.status_code == 429:
        time.sleep(int(resp.headers.get('Retry-After', 1)) * (2 ** attempt))
    else:
        break
```
samir: FYI metrics team asked that we don't embed raw panel IDs in public docs. Replace them with a token `{{panel_link}}` that resolves to the right dashboard mapping (internal) and link to the public dashboard via friendly name. I pinged infra about a stable redirect.
alex: ack — swapping IDs for tokens. Will put a note in docs about why we avoid raw IDs.
ciara: tagging @ops-infra in the PR thread might help get the redirect faster.
maya: LGTM. alex, can you add a docs-test for the snippet? We have the `docs-tests` runner that executes code blocks via `doctest` harness.
alex: Yep. Adding a small unit test that runs the snippet against the `docs-test` mock endpoint.
li: One more: localization. The i18n extractor already captured the old strings in several locales; we need to bump the extraction so translators get the updated phrasing. Mark strings for extraction with `_()` macro.
jordan: Good catch. I'll update the i18n note in the PR.
alex: PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/827 (added checklist, backoff snippet, tokens, doctest). Tests pass locally. Can someone queue CI?
maya: Queued. CI log: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/827 — looks like linter failing on trailing spaces in a code block.
samir: Fixed in a follow-up commit, pushed.
ciara: All green on staging preview. I spot-checked the staging page: /docs/staging/usage-tiers and the example payloads render correctly.
docs-bot: deploy to staging docs successful — https://staging.docs.redwood.ai/usage/usage-tiers
alex: Verifying staging now. Screenshot: panel text updated, tokens replaced, and the sample snippet passes `doctest`.
maya: After merge, remember to add a short line in the release notes: "Usage tier consolidation: split metering and pricing pages; updated SDK examples and dashboard link tokens."
alex: Added to release notes in PR.
ciara: Merged. :tada:
alex: Thanks all — closing follow-ups: I'll create a tiny follow-up to add a cross-link from the billing FAQ to the migration guide.
maya: Thanks Alex.
alex: Done. Closing thread.
